info.title: modama API
info.summary: Management interface API for the ER-C data management system.
info.description:
The API behind the new management interface. The legacy `/api/` endpoints are
a separate API, which stays frozen for existing clients.

### Versioning

Every request must state the contract version it was written against, as a bare
integer in the `X-Modama-API-Version` header. There is no default: a request
without the header is rejected, so a deploy cannot silently move an installed
client onto a newer contract. Currently supported: 1.

The resolved version is echoed on the response, together with
`X-Modama-API-Versions-Supported`. A deprecated version is announced with
`Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers before it is switched off. `GET /versions`
lists the same information and can be called before pinning a version.

### Errors

Errors use HTTP status codes with a body of `{"code", "message"}`. Clients
can branch on `code`, which is stable; `message` is meant for display. The one
exception is HTTP 422, which carries FastAPI's own field-level `detail` list for
a malformed request body.

### Authentication

`POST /auth/login` sets an `HttpOnly` session cookie, which the browser sends
back automatically. A session ends after a period of inactivity and after an
absolute limit; `"persistent": true` on login drops the idle timeout in exchange
for a longer absolute limit ("keep me logged in"). State-changing requests are
also checked against the request `Origin`. Endpoints that need a session are
marked with a lock below.

### Creating things

The `POST` endpoints that create a project, a session or an ingest share are
idempotent: the first request answers `201` with the new resource, and a repeat
of the same request answers `200` with the existing one instead of an error. A
client that lost a response to a flaky network can therefore simply send the
request again. The only conflict (`409`) is a project of the same name that
belongs to someone else.

### Changing things

`PUT /projects/{project}/members` takes the complete member list wanted,
not operations; the API works out what to add and remove, so a retry is safe.
Sealing a session that is sealed already answers `200` with the session as it
is. `DELETE /ingest-shares/{share_id}` answers `204`, and `404` once the
share is gone.

A project or session description is the text of a `README.md` in its folder,
`null` when there is none. It can be given on create and changed with
`PUT .../description`; an empty text removes the file. The file is written over
WebDAV as the signed-in user, so the file system decides who may change it:
whoever created it. People can also edit the file directly; whatever it says is
shown.

### Slow calls

`GET /projects/{project}/usage` runs `du` over the project and can take a
minute on a large one. Nothing else waits for it: the project details answer
with `usage_bytes` null.

### Browsing

`GET /browse?path=…` lists a folder of the data tree one page at a time:
`entries` holds up to `limit` of them (200 by default, 1000 at most), folders
first and then by name, and `next_cursor` fetches the page after it, until it
is null. The cursor marks the last entry seen rather than an offset, so an
entry added or removed while paging neither repeats nor hides another. The
listing is made as the signed-in user and shows what that user may see.

post.summary: Sign in and receive a session cookie
post.description:
Sign in. A normal session ends after a period of inactivity and after an
absolute limit. With `persistent: true` there is no idle timeout and the
absolute limit is the longer, persistent one.

post.summary: Create a project, or return it if it already exists
post.description:
Create an ad-hoc project owned by the signed-in user.

Idempotent: sending the same request again answers 200 with the existing
project instead of an error, so a client that lost the first response can
simply retry. Only a project that belongs to someone else is a conflict.
The existing project is returned as it is; changing its members or its
description is a separate operation.

A `description` is saved as `README.md` in the project folder, owned by
the signed-in user. It is written over WebDAV once the folder exists; if
that fails, the project stays and the answer is a 502.

put.summary: Set the members of a project
put.description:
Replace the members of a project with the given list.

The API works out who to add and who to remove against the current
members, so the client sends the list it wants rather than operations.
Sending the same list again changes nothing and answers with the project
as it is, which also makes a retry after a lost or partial answer safe:
the difference is computed afresh each time. The owner is a member
whatever the list says and is never added or removed.

post.summary: Create a session in a project, or return it if it already exists
post.description:
Create a session folder in a project, as the signed-in user.

Idempotent: a session that already exists is answered with 200 and its
current state instead of an error, so a client that lost the first
response can simply retry. A session has no owner of its own; any member
of the project gets the existing one back. Its description is returned as
it is; the one in the request is not applied (see `PUT .../description`).

A `description` is saved as `README.md` in the session folder, next to
`raw/`, owned by the signed-in user. It is written over WebDAV once the
folder exists; if that fails, the session stays and the answer is a 502.

post.summary: Seal a session: make its raw data immutable

cannot be undone through the API.

Idempotent: a session that is already sealed is answered with 200 and its
current state, without asking the permissions service again. The rest of
the session folder stays writable; only `raw/` is sealed.

post.summary: Open an ingest share for a session, or return the one already open
post.description:
Open a share for a session that writes as the signed-in user.

Idempotent per user and session: if the signed-in user already has a share
for that session, it is answered with 200 instead of a second share, so a
client that lost the first response can simply retry. Another user's share
for the same session is not reused; each user ingests under their own
identity.

modama-agent also sends `X-Agent-Token` and `resource`, which bind the share
to the agent's resource, so that smbdrop offers the share to that
resource's agents. The token must have been issued for that `resource`. A
repeat then counts only a share bound to the same resource: a user can have
one share per session at each resource.

parameters.name: X-Agent-Token

schema.description: Token from smbdrop's token service, which modama-agent fetches with its client certificate. It says which resource the request comes from; the session still says who the user is. Sent together with `resource` in the body, or not at all.

goes away. The data written through it stays in the session.

Only the user who opened a share can close it. A share that is gone
already is a 404; a client that lost the answer to its first attempt can
treat that as closed.

get.summary: List a folder of the data tree, one page at a time
get.description:
The file or folder at `path`, with the links to open it elsewhere, and for
a folder one page of its entries.

Pages are keyed, not offset: the cursor marks the last entry of the page
before, so the next page starts after it whatever was added to or removed
from the folder in between, and no entry repeats or goes missing. The
cursor is opaque, and it does not depend on `limit`.

The listing is made as the signed-in user, so it shows what that user may
see. The file server cannot page, so each page lists the whole folder on
the server; that costs well under a second even for a folder of tens of
thousands of entries.

get.description:
The contract versions this server supports.

Unauthenticated and unversioned on purpose: a locally installed client
calls this at startup, before it has a session or knows which version to
use. That way it can report a problem in its own log, where the person
running the instrument sees it, instead of failing in the middle of an
ingest later.

reference the same schema from every operation and a generated client gets
one error type instead of one per endpoint.

created_by.description: Login name of the user who opened the share. Null for shares opened before this was recorded.

smb_host.title: Smb Host
smb_host.description: Samba host as seen from the intranet, for a person connecting by hand. modama-agent uses its own configured host instead.

workgroup.title: Workgroup
workgroup.description: Workgroup for the username on Windows, for connecting by hand.

IngestShare.title: IngestShare
IngestShare.description:
An ingest share. The fields smbdrop reports, plus the project and session
it belongs to, so that a client does not parse `dest_path`, and the host
and workgroup the web interface shows a person who connects by hand.
modama-agent does not use those two: an instrument computer may reach the Samba
server another way than the intranet does, so the agent mounts with the
host, port and domain from its own configuration file.

shares.title: Shares
shares.description: The signed-in user's open shares, oldest first.

rsync.title: Rsync
rsync.description: An rsync command that pushes to the path.

sftp.title: Sftp
sftp.description: An sftp command that opens the path's folder.

smb_windows.title: Smb Windows
smb_windows.description: The path on the Samba share, as a UNC path.

smb_unix.title: Smb Unix
smb_unix.description: The path on the Samba share, as an smb:// URL.

LocationAccess.title: LocationAccess
LocationAccess.description: The entry links plus the transfer commands for the browsed path.

persistent.title: Persistent
persistent.description: Keep the session without an idle timeout, up to the configured persistent lifetime. For the UI's "keep me logged in" and for long-running clients such as modama-agent.

description.title: Description
description.description: The text of the project folder's `README.md`, or null when there is none.

Project.title: Project
Project.description:
One project, in the shape the permissions service returns.

The fields are identical to those of the legacy `/api/project/` response, so
that screens can migrate one endpoint at a time without changing how they
read a project. `usage_bytes` is null everywhere but in the answer of
`GET /projects/{project}/usage`: computing it means a `du` over the whole
project, which nothing else should wait for.

description.title: Description
description.description: The text of the project folder's `README.md`, or null when there is none.

ProjectDetails.title: ProjectDetails
ProjectDetails.description: A project with its sessions. `usage_bytes` is null; see `GET .../usage`.

usage_bytes.title: Usage Bytes
usage_bytes.description: Disk usage of the project folder in bytes, as `du` reports it.

immutable.title: Immutable
immutable.description: True once the session has been sealed: its `raw/` folder is immutable.

description.title: Description
description.description: The text of the session folder's `README.md`, next to `raw/`, or null when there is none.

Session.title: Session
Session.description: One session, in the shape the project details of the legacy API use.

persistent.title: Persistent
persistent.description: Whether the session was opened with `persistent: true`.

description.title: Description
description.description: The new description, saved as `README.md` in the folder. An empty text, or one of only whitespace, removes the file.
examples: Off-axis holography of Ni nanowires, Titan G2, Feb 2026.

members.title: Members
members.description: The complete list of members wanted. Members not in it are removed, names not yet members are added. The owner is a member regardless and may be left out.

users.title: Users
users.description: Usernames of everyone who may use the data management system, sorted. These are the accounts a project can have as members.

session.description: Signed session cookie, set by `POST /auth/login` and sent back automatically by the browser. Requests without a usable one get 401.
session.name: __Host-modama_session
